title: Explore the employee export and build the employee view
prompt:
The people team wants payroll and reporting-line numbers from the HR system. Everything starts from the `employees` table: 221 people, typed in by hand over the years. Look at it first: inside your function, add `employees.printSchema()` and `print(employees.count())`, then press Run.

Then write `employee_view(employees)`. It returns the columns the pipeline uses, in order, with one `full_name` in place of the two name columns. Every row stays, messy values and all: this step only shapes the columns.
rules: Leave the salary out: pay comes from the salary history in a later step.
Every row of `employees` is still there, unchanged, even repeated or odd ones.
hints: `select` picks columns in the order you list them.
`F.concat_ws(" ", "first_name", "last_name")` joins the two names with a space. Give it a name with `.alias("full_name")`.
Don't clean or filter anything yet. The text is fixed in the next step.
explanation: `select` both picks and orders the columns, and `F.concat_ws(" ", "first_name", "last_name").alias("full_name")` builds the name the reports show. The `salary` column is left out on purpose: it's only the latest salary the system knows, while payroll needs the salary in force on a given date, which comes from the history. Nothing is filtered yet, so later checks can count every problem row.
starter:
